conclusion: XGBoost performance gains differed substantially between demand types.
numerical_evidence: Mean WRMSSE improvements over seasonal naive were 21.130% for smooth, 16.443% for erratic, 0.503% for intermittent and 10.439% for lumpy demand.
reporting_caution: Report results separately by demand type rather than presenting one universal model effect.

conclusion: XGBoost was the strongest primary forecasting model under the evaluated design.
numerical_evidence: XGBoost produced the lowest mean WRMSSE for all four demand types and beat seasonal naive in 5 of 5 smooth folds, 5 of 5 erratic folds, 4 of 5 intermittent folds and 4 of 5 lumpy folds.
reporting_caution: Do not describe the fold counts as evidence of statistical significance.

conclusion: XGBoost provided only a small WRMSSE improvement for intermittent demand.
numerical_evidence: Mean WRMSSE decreased from 1.215647 to 1.209538, an improvement of 0.503%.
reporting_caution: Do not generalise the stronger smooth and erratic results to intermittent demand.

conclusion: Rolling features dominated complete-model SHAP reliance for every demand type.
numerical_evidence: Mean rolling-group SHAP shares were 69.708% for smooth, 66.267% for erratic, 70.840% for intermittent and 72.190% for lumpy demand.
reporting_caution: SHAP measures model reliance and does not establish forecast benefit or causality.

conclusion: Calendar features provided the clearest positive ablation evidence for smooth and erratic demand.
numerical_evidence: Removing calendar features increased mean WRMSSE by 0.125891 for smooth and 0.113205 for erratic demand.
reporting_caution: Ablation values are conditional on the locked non-retuned model configuration.

conclusion: Lag and event/SNAP feature groups did not improve mean intermittent-demand WRMSSE under the locked setup.
numerical_evidence: Removing lag features improved WRMSSE in all five folds with mean ΔWRMSSE -0.073589. Removing event/SNAP features improved four of five folds with mean ΔWRMSSE -0.050043.
reporting_caution: Do not interpret this as proof that these variables are inherently unhelpful for intermittent demand.

conclusion: Price and event/SNAP information provided the most consistent positive ablation evidence for lumpy demand.
numerical_evidence: Removing price increased mean WRMSSE by 0.094992, and removing event/SNAP increased it by 0.075897. Both removals worsened all five folds.
reporting_caution: These are conditional predictive contributions, not causal effects.

conclusion: The sequence-only LSTM did not improve hierarchical forecast performance.
numerical_evidence: LSTM mean WRMSSE was 0.927770 for smooth and 1.251330 for erratic demand, which was 45.879% and 57.643% worse than XGBoost respectively.
reporting_caution: The LSTM and XGBoost used different information sets, so this is not an isolated architecture comparison.

conclusion: The LSTM disadvantage was substantially greater at aggregate hierarchy levels.
numerical_evidence: Relative to XGBoost, LSTM level-normalised WRMSSE was 122.060% worse at smooth Level 1 and 8.020% worse at Level 12. The corresponding erratic gaps were 156.940% and 20.411%.
reporting_caution: Describe the aggregation pattern without making a causal claim about why it occurred.
